decisions.executionNote: Raise left arm in elbow-up approach and begin orienting toward the left tube; right arm stays parked.
Continue left approach with smaller rotation and translation increments after continuity guard; align above tube.
Bring left gripper vertically above the tube body and align jaws transverse to its axis.
Lower around left tube with small wrist-image centering correction, then close gripper fully.
Lift the closed left grasp clear of the table, with a small retreat before rotating upright.
Tube remains between fingers in wrist view; rotate it toward upright while carrying toward the left rack slot.
Continue slow upright rotation and translate over the left side of the rack without crossing the midline.
Finish upright orientation and align the tube above a left rack opening, staying at clearance height.
Lower the upright left tube into the aligned left opening while retaining the grasp.
Seat the first tube to depth, pause, and open the left gripper for release.
Withdraw the open left gripper to check whether the tube has settled upright and fully into the rack.
The first tube did not remain upright. Clear the left arm for recovery later and begin an elbow-up approach to the rightmost tube.
Advance the right arm above the rightmost tube and continue its downward grasp orientation; retreat left toward home.
Complete right downward alignment above the tube body; continue returning the open left arm without changing elbow branch.
Lower right gripper around the tube and correct the remaining in-plane axis angle; finish parking left.
Center right grasp slightly toward the cap, then close fully around the tube body and pause.
Lift the retained right tube clear of the table before turning upright; keep the left arm parked.
Carry the right tube inward while slowly rotating it upright, maintaining clearance above the rack.
Continue right-tube transport and upright rotation in small continuous increments.
Finish turning the right tube upright above the rack, then inspect alignment before insertion.
Correct the right tube slightly inward over the front-right large hole and lower toward its entrance.
Advance a few millimeters toward the hole center and lower slowly, checking seating before release.
Tube appears to contact the rim rather than enter. Lift clear and shift slightly right and back to recenter before retrying.
Nudge the upright tube rightward over the visible right-side large opening, then make a slow insertion retry.
Continue the centered insertion slowly to account for the tube having shifted upward within the grasp; keep closed until seated.
Open gently at the apparent seated depth, then withdraw a short distance to inspect whether the tube stays upright.
The released right tube is upright in the rack. Clear the open right gripper to prepare for the remaining right-side tube.
Orient the open right gripper down toward the remaining right tube, approaching at clearance height.
Continue gradual right-wrist reorientation over the loose tube with the gripper open and table clearance maintained.
Finish the downward grasp orientation and center over the remaining loose right tube.
Lower around the loose tube body with a small axis correction and close the right gripper.
Allow the grasp to close, then lift the remaining right tube clear while keeping its orientation fixed.
Begin rotating the held tube upright while carrying it toward a separate central rack slot, above the inserted tube.
Continue upright rotation and inward transport of the second tube, keeping clearance from the seated tube.
Finish the upright orientation over a central opening, separated from the seated rightmost tube.
Recenter the upright tube over the central front-row opening and lower to just above the entrance.
Lower the centered second tube toward seated depth, keeping its upright orientation and grasp closed.
Seat the central tube a few millimeters farther, release, and begin a short withdrawal for visual verification.
Both released tubes remain upright. Withdraw right and start a left elbow-up approach to recover the fallen tube in front of the rack.
Advance left above the fallen tube, with jaws across its body; return the open right arm toward home.
The fallen tube's cap faces forward; reorient the left wrist above it to match that direction while finishing right-arm retreat.
Continue turning the left gripper to match the forward-facing cap, approaching above the loose tube without crossing the midline.
Complete left wrist alignment with the fallen tube's cap direction and lower to a safe pregrasp height.
Lower the aligned left gripper around the fallen tube, slightly toward its cap and away from the rack.
Close around the recovered tube and begin a cautious lift away from the rack.
Lift the recovered tube higher and retreat left to provide clear space for its upright rotation.
Begin a slow continuous rotation of the recovered tube toward upright, holding it clear to the left of the rack.
Continue the recovered tube's upright rotation, slowly moving toward the empty left rack opening.
Continue the smooth left-wrist rotation toward upright, holding the tube above the unoccupied left side.
Finish upright orientation and move the recovered tube farther back over the empty left opening, correcting the earlier front-edge miss.
Make a small leftward centering correction and lower the recovered upright tube toward the vacant left slot.
